pathway.title: APi Group Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The strongest support is earnings momentum in a diversified business. Nine-month adjusted EBITDA rose 20.11% to USD 896 million, trailing reported EBITDA reached USD 998 million, no customer exceeded 5% of revenue in 2025, and mandated inspection work gives recurring demand, although the recurring share is not quantified. Growth lowers leverage only if it persists, because the added debt is already on the balance sheet. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation CALC-5

The weakest dimension is leverage after debt-funded acquisitions. Net debt rose by USD 1,354 million to USD 3,201 million in nine months, taking net debt to 3.21x trailing reported EBITDA from 2.10x at the 2025 year end and total debt to 3.58x from 3.13x; on adjusted EBITDA the figures are 3.00x total and 2.69x net. Acquisitions and buybacks totalled USD 1,608 million against free cash flow of USD 317 million, so the gap was borrowed or taken from cash. The USD 100 million borrowed on the revolver and the USD 143 million of shares repurchased after quarter end are not reflected, and their effect on net debt is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-14

Interest cover looks strong but is flattered by timing. Trailing EBITDA covers cash interest 7.74x, yet cash interest paid lags the expense, and third-quarter interest expense of USD 45 million is above its year-earlier USD 34 million. On trailing net interest expense cover is 6.98x, and on the third-quarter run rate it is 5.54x, so cover is likely to fall toward the lower figures as the 2034 notes pay a full year of interest. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-9

Liquidity is adequate but thinner and more dependent on the revolver. Cash and undrawn revolver fell from USD 1,657 million at 2025 year end to USD 1,032 million, and the revolver is 33.50% drawn against a 30% usage level above which a first lien net leverage test with a maximum of 3.75x applies; the issuer reports 1.6x at quarter end, wide against that maximum, but the covenant definitions are not supplied, so the reported figure cannot be tied to the leverage computed here. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4

Cash conversion has weakened as working capital absorbs growth. Free cash flow was 35.38% of adjusted EBITDA in nine months against 41.15%, the working capital outflow was USD 312 million against USD 218 million, and the gross margin fell to 30.82% from 31.22% on mix and material costs. This is the first place a slowdown in contracting work would show, because customer advances of USD 902 million would unwind if billings slowed. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-7; calculation CALC-9; calculation CALC-11

Refinancing capacity rests on a long-dated maturity profile and a recent successful issue rather than on current ratings. No scheduled maturity of size falls before 2029, when USD 614 million of senior notes mature, and USD 500 million of 2034 notes were placed in May 2026, but the balance sheet classes USD 361 million of debt as current at 2026-09-30 against USD 5 million at the 2025 year end and the filings do not break it down; the only rating statement is a 2025 note giving BB and Ba2 as stable, and no agency report or market price is supplied. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; calculation CALC-8; calculation CALC-14

Financial policy risk is medium. Acquisitions and buybacks raise leverage while cash payouts to shareholders stay modest and the Series A dividend is settled in shares, but a further USD 143 million of shares was repurchased in October while the revolver was drawn a further USD 100 million, and the legal capacity for distributions and acquisitions cannot be tested without the credit agreement. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation CALC-14

runs.text: Credit strengths are the diversified, inspection-led service model, earnings momentum and a long-dated maturity profile. The service model spreads revenue across two segments, many customers and several countries, and inspection work is often required by law or insurance, which supports demand through a downturn; nine-month adjusted EBITDA growth of 20.11% shows that demand is converting into earnings. Debt matures late, with USD 614 million due in 2029, USD 335 million of revolver in 2031, USD 2,147 million of term loan in 2033 and USD 500 million of notes in 2034, so scheduled refinancing pressure is distant. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-8

Credit weaknesses are rising leverage, thinner liquidity and weaker cash conversion. Net leverage of 3.21x against 2.10x at the year end reflects acquisitions and buybacks funded by debt and cash; liquidity fell by USD 625 million; and free cash flow conversion fell as working capital grew. A related weakness is the lack of evidence on legal capacity and ownership, which leaves the limits on further distributions and borrowing unknown. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-6

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: In 2026 the company completed three large acquisitions in its Safety Services segment and ten smaller ones. CertaSite, a United States inspection-first fire and life safety provider, closed on 2026-02-02 for consideration of USD 271 million, of which USD 268 million was paid in cash at closing. Onyx-Fire Protection Services, a Canadian provider bought from funds managed by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities under an agreement signed on 2026-04-22 for about C$725 in cash, closed on 2026-06-08; the second-quarter report states consideration of USD 522 million and the third-quarter report USD 532 million, a difference of USD 10 million that is not explained. WTech Fire Group, a European fire sprinkler, suppression and detection provider agreed on 2026-04-17 for about EUR 324 in cash, closed on 2026-07-01 for about USD 394 million in cash. The ten smaller acquisitions cost USD 227 million, of which USD 36 million is accrued consideration. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2026-03-31_apg-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-06-30_apg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_apg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36

New debt in the period comprised USD 500 million of 5.750% senior notes due 2034, issued by the borrower subsidiary on 2026-05-14 with the net proceeds used for general corporate purposes including funding the announced acquisitions, and the Ninth Amendment to the credit agreement of the same date, which raised the revolver from USD 750 million to USD 1,000 million, lifted the letter of credit sublimit from USD 250 million to USD 300 million, and extended the revolver to 2031-05-14 and the term loan to 2033-05-14. The revolver was drawn USD 335 million at 2026-09-30 and a further USD 100 million after quarter end. These debt facts are stated here as transaction context only; their effect on leverage is for Financial foundation. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 10-Q_2026-06-30_apg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 65

fields.value: Financial foundation for APi Group Corp (issuer id apg), as of 2026-11-05, on the Full credit assessment pathway. It sets out consolidated annual and interim statements, leverage, interest cover, liquidity and debt for FY2024, FY2025 and the first nine months of 2026, on the registrant's consolidated perimeter in USD millions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions and share repurchases lifted leverage in 2026: total debt reached 3.58x trailing reported EBITDA and net debt 3.21x at 2026-09-30, against 3.13x and 2.10x at the 2025 year end, while liquidity fell to USD 1,032 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover rose to 7.74x as earnings grew and cash interest paid fell, but interest expense in the third quarter of 2026 was USD 45 million against USD 34 million a year earlier. The USD 100 million drawn on the revolver after quarter end is not reflected in net debt, and its effect on net debt is not established. Trailing EBITDA carries acquired businesses only from their closing dates and the filings state no pro forma earnings, so run-rate leverage is not established.

A partial revolver repayment from operating cash flow, or disclosed pro forma earnings for the acquisitions, would move the view toward lower leverage; further debt-funded acquisitions or a larger working capital outflow would move it the other way.

fields.value: The business is diversified by service line, geography and customer, and its largest dependency is Safety Services. Life Safety was 67.14% of nine-month 2026 net revenues, the United States invoiced 67.66% of them, and no single customer exceeded 5% of 2025 net revenues. About half of employees are covered by collective bargaining agreements, which limits how quickly labour cost can be cut in a downturn even though management describes its cost structure as highly variable. Mandated inspection work gives recurring demand in principle, but the share of revenue that recurs is not quantified, so cash-flow durability rests on management's own description.

fields.value: Acquisitions are the dominant driver of change and are paid for in cash at closing. In 2026 the three large acquisitions cost USD 271 million, USD 532 million and USD 394 million, and ten smaller ones cost USD 227 million, so the year's acquisition spending reached USD 1,424 million before any acquired earnings. The filings state no pro forma earnings or purchase multiples, so the leverage effect of these purchases cannot be sized from this module's evidence, and the seller of the largest was funds managed by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities. In May the company issued USD 500 million of 2034 senior notes and enlarged its revolver to help fund the later purchases.

fields.value: Ownership is not disclosed in the supplied documents beyond one equity-linked instrument that matters to creditors. The Series A preferred, held through a vehicle controlled by a board co-chair, entitles its holder to an annual dividend equal to 20% of the rise in the share price above its previous high-water mark, applied to a fixed block of shares, which was USD 590 million for 2025 and was settled in new shares in January 2026. The dividend is payable in shares or cash at the board's election and the company states it intends to use shares, so the mechanism is dilution today; a cash election would create a large claim that ranks ahead of common equity, and the 2026 dividend and conversion into common shares fall at the end of 2026. A related entity of a co-chair also receives advisory fees of USD 4 million a year, which is small but is cash paid to a shareholder-linked party.

fields.value: Financial policy favours growth over deleveraging while keeping cash distributions limited. No cash dividend is paid on common shares and the credit agreement restricts distributions in some situations, but the company has USD 750 million of buyback authorisation remaining after repurchasing about USD 250 million in the nine months of 2026 and USD 75 million in 2025, and in 2024 it paid USD 600 million to repurchase half of the shares from the converted Series B preferred, partly funded by a USD 300 million incremental term loan. Buybacks alongside debt-funded acquisitions raise leverage, and the legal capacity for further distributions is not established because the credit agreement is not supplied.

fields.value: The finance function has changed recently and its systems are in transition. The chief executive has led the company since 2004, but the chief financial officer has held the role since March 2025 after serving as interim from December 2024, the principal accounting officer designation moved to the chief financial officer from August 2026, and a series of enterprise system implementations began in 2026 with the review of internal controls under way. This matters because reporting reliability underpins monitoring, and because systems and business enablement costs are being added back to adjusted earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure supports monitoring of results but not of structure. Segment, geography and revenue-line data are given every quarter, but guarantor information, a list of subsidiary guarantors, covenant certificates and the proxy statement are not in the supplied set, and customer contract terms are not described beyond general statements. Creditors can follow operating performance but cannot confirm which entities stand behind the debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that value going to shareholders has mostly been settled in shares or has been small: no cash dividend on common shares, a Series A dividend settled in shares, advisory fees of only USD 4 million a year, and USD 458 million of equity raised in 2024 to help fund the Elevated acquisition. The company has also used amendments to extend maturities and enlarge the revolver rather than to weaken creditor terms, as far as the supplied summaries show. A move to cash settlement of the Series A dividend, repurchases that exceed free cash flow for a sustained period, or a further large acquisition paid mainly in debt would move the view toward higher governance and financial-policy risk. Disclosure of ownership percentages, pro forma acquired earnings and the credit agreement's distribution limits would reduce the uncertainty in either direction.

fields.value: Fundamental credit for APi Group Corp (issuer id apg), as of 2026-11-05, on the Full credit assessment pathway. It synthesises the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance work into one creditor view of the issuer's strengths, weaknesses, downside path and monitoring triggers, using the seven supplied issuer documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: APi Group's credit profile is adequate but weakening: strong earnings growth in a diversified, inspection-led business has been matched by debt-funded acquisitions that lifted net leverage to 3.21x and cut liquidity, so creditors bear integration and cash-conversion risk until acquired earnings arrive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is a squeeze on project margins and working capital while the revolver stays drawn and buybacks continue. Net debt of USD 3,201 million at 2026-09-30 excludes a USD 100 million revolver borrowing and a USD 143 million share repurchase after quarter end, and their effect on net debt is not established. Governance and financial-policy risk is at a medium level, and rating, market and legal-document evidence is absent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest support is earnings momentum in a diversified business. Nine-month adjusted EBITDA rose 20.11% to USD 896 million, trailing reported EBITDA reached USD 998 million, no customer exceeded 5% of revenue in 2025, and mandated inspection work gives recurring demand, although the recurring share is not quantified. Growth lowers leverage only if it persists, because the added debt is already on the balance sheet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The weakest dimension is leverage after debt-funded acquisitions. Net debt rose by USD 1,354 million to USD 3,201 million in nine months, taking net debt to 3.21x trailing reported EBITDA from 2.10x at the 2025 year end and total debt to 3.58x from 3.13x; on adjusted EBITDA the figures are 3.00x total and 2.69x net. Acquisitions and buybacks totalled USD 1,608 million against free cash flow of USD 317 million, so the gap was borrowed or taken from cash. The USD 100 million borrowed on the revolver and the USD 143 million of shares repurchased after quarter end are not reflected, and their effect on net debt is not established.

fields.value: Interest cover looks strong but is flattered by timing. Trailing EBITDA covers cash interest 7.74x, yet cash interest paid lags the expense, and third-quarter interest expense of USD 45 million is above its year-earlier USD 34 million. On trailing net interest expense cover is 6.98x, and on the third-quarter run rate it is 5.54x, so cover is likely to fall toward the lower figures as the 2034 notes pay a full year of interest.

fields.value: Liquidity is adequate but thinner and more dependent on the revolver. Cash and undrawn revolver fell from USD 1,657 million at 2025 year end to USD 1,032 million, and the revolver is 33.50% drawn against a 30% usage level above which a first lien net leverage test with a maximum of 3.75x applies; the issuer reports 1.6x at quarter end, wide against that maximum, but the covenant definitions are not supplied, so the reported figure cannot be tied to the leverage computed here.

This is the first place a slowdown in contracting work would show, because customer advances of USD 902 million would unwind if billings slowed.

fields.value: Financial policy risk is medium. Acquisitions and buybacks raise leverage while cash payouts to shareholders stay modest and the Series A dividend is settled in shares, but a further USD 143 million of shares was repurchased in October while the revolver was drawn a further USD 100 million, and the legal capacity for distributions and acquisitions cannot be tested without the credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is that trailing figures include acquired businesses only from their closing dates, so leverage of 3.21x net may overstate the run-rate, and that earnings have grown 20.11% in nine months with no maturity pressure until 2029. If acquired earnings are disclosed and are material, or if the revolver is repaid from operating cash flow, leverage could fall toward the year-end level. The strongest evidence for a worse view is that interest cover on current expense is lower than on cash paid, that free cash flow conversion fell, and that the legal limits on further debt-funded buybacks and acquisitions are unknown. A further large debt-funded acquisition, a rise in revolver use, or a margin fall below the current 30.82% would move the view toward weaker credit quality.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Credit strengths are the diversified, inspection-led service model, earnings momentum and a long-dated maturity profile. The service model spreads revenue across two segments, many customers and several countries, and inspection work is often required by law or insurance, which supports demand through a downturn; nine-month adjusted EBITDA growth of 20.11% shows that demand is converting into earnings. Debt matures late, with USD 614 million due in 2029, USD 335 million of revolver in 2031, USD 2,147 million of term loan in 2033 and USD 500 million of notes in 2034, so scheduled refinancing pressure is distant.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Credit weaknesses are rising leverage, thinner liquidity and weaker cash conversion. Net leverage of 3.21x against 2.10x at the year end reflects acquisitions and buybacks funded by debt and cash; liquidity fell by USD 625 million; and free cash flow conversion fell as working capital grew. A related weakness is the lack of evidence on legal capacity and ownership, which leaves the limits on further distributions and borrowing unknown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with slower contracting demand or higher tariff-driven material costs. Growth is concentrated in the lower-margin Specialty Services segment, which is 32.92% of revenue, grew 26.63% in nine months against 13.07% for Safety Services and earns a segment margin of 10.87% against 16.74%, so a slowdown there would be expected to hit earnings and working capital first. Lower volume and margin reduce earnings and leave working capital tied up, so free cash flow weakens while acquisition integration costs and buybacks continue; the revolver then funds the gap, undrawn liquidity falls below its current USD 1,032 million, and revolver use stays above the 30% level at which the first lien test applies. Management has levers: buybacks are discretionary with USD 607 million of authorisation remaining at 2026-10-29, acquisitions can be paused, and capital expenditures are typically below 1.5% of revenue, although about half of employees are covered by collective bargaining agreements, which limits discretion over labour cost. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid distress in a moderate downturn because no scheduled maturity of size falls due before 2029, but the reported covenant headroom is wide and has not been tested independently.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months, tailwinds are regulation-driven inspection demand, infrastructure and technology end markets and the 20.11% earnings growth already shown; headwinds are tariffs, material cost and the integration of three large acquisitions. Management raised full-year guidance for net revenues and adjusted EBITDA in each of the three 2026 releases, to USD 1,235 million to USD 1,255 million of adjusted EBITDA in the latest, but lowered its adjusted free cash flow conversion guidance to 110% from 115% of adjusted net income. The guidance supports the near-term earnings view and is management outlook, not evidence, and the lower conversion guidance fits the weaker cash conversion shown above.
